subject: Post-demo recap & evaluation plan — Streaming stop-sequence/latency notes

Subject: Post-demo recap & evaluation plan — Streaming stop-sequence/latency notes

Hi Jane / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum:

Summary of what we heard from you:
- Primary use case: multi-turn clinical note generation from visit transcripts (short to medium length, 300–2,000 tokens).
- Key constraints: must avoid mid-sentence truncations in streaming UI, robust stop-sequence handling (clinic-specific templates), and 95th-percentile latency < 600ms for single-user interactive flows.
- Success criteria for POC: quality parity with your current rule-based system on templated sections, no clinically misleading partial outputs, and clear cost guidance.

Recommended evaluation plan (short):
1) Models to test (suggested order):
   - rw-instruct-7b-q4f32 (low-latency, quantized; good for fast interactive flows)
   - rw-rlhf-13b (higher quality for summarization-heavy prompts)
   - rw-stream-13b-8k (optimized kernel for streaming coherence at longer contexts)
2) Prompt & stop-set: attached acme-promptset-v1.json (includes stop tokens and template prompts you used in demo).
3) Benchmarks: we created a quick harness and uploaded results -> redwood-eval-benchmarks.csv (attached). Our initial run shows median token latency ~28ms on dedicated capacity for rw-instruct-7b-q4f32; 95th percentile ~540ms for rw-rlhf-13b at 2k context when batching is disabled.
4) Streaming-specific checks: partial-token coherence (check for mid-token/phrase repetition), stop-sequence enforcement under streaming (edge case: stop across chunk boundary), and behavior under jittered network conditions.

Immediate asks from us:
- Can you upload a redacted sample set (5–10 transcripts) into the shared Drive folder referenced below? We’ll run the initial prompt set and return a prioritized defect list.
- Any hard constraints for stop tokens besides the templates in the prompt set? (e.g., must stop on "

Final:" or a clinician signature)

Next steps / timeline:
- By Mon 5/24: Acme uploads redacted transcripts.
- By Wed 5/26: Redwood returns bench report + short list of streaming anomalies with suggested mitigations.
- Week of 6/1: Joint call for results + production alignment.

Attachments: acme-promptset-v1.json, acme-demo-recording.mp4, redwood-eval-benchmarks.csv

Link to evals: https://redwood-inference.app/evals/RDW-4781

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the Drive link and a calendar invite for the week of 6/1 once we see the sample uploads.

Thanks Soojin — this is very helpful. Two quick clarifications from our side:
1) During the demo we saw a couple of partial outputs where the model started a sentence, then later the UI appended an overlapping fragment (made it look like the sentence duplicated). Is that something you expect to see with streaming?
2) Stop sequences are critical — our templates include both literal tokens ("---END---") and more semantic cues ("Doctor:") that sometimes appear mid-response. Will the streaming path honor those immediately, or is there a post-processing step that can delay enforcement?

We’ll upload the 6 redacted transcripts to the Drive by Monday. Also looped Tom so procurement stays aware of the timeline.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Jane Slater <jane.slater@acmehealth.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & Evaluation plan — Streaming stop-sequence/latency notes

Jane — great questions. Short answers up front, then a concrete test plan: 

1) Partial-overlap / duplication in streaming:
   - What you saw is a common surface symptom when client-side reassembly overlaps chunks or when the model emits a partial phrase that is later completed with slightly different tokenization. In our runtime we stream token deltas; the client must append deterministically.
   - Mitigations we will run in the POC: enforce idempotent chunk framing on the client, enable server-side dedupe heuristics for repeated prefix tokens, and try rw-stream-13b-8k which reduces cross-chunk repetition in our internal tests.

2) Stop-sequence enforcement in streaming:
   - Redwood supports two mechanisms: immediate soft-stop (streaming stops as soon as stop token is seen) and strict-stop (server truncates output and prunes KV cache to avoid leaks). Strict-stop has negligible extra latency but can change how partial tokens look in the last 1–2 chunks.
   - For your semantic cues ("Doctor:"), we recommend adding both literal and normalized forms to the stop-set and enabling strict-stop for clinical template sections. We’ll include a test case where stop spans a chunk boundary.

Concrete POC tests we’ll run once we have samples:
- Test A (streaming coherence): 6 transcripts, compare rw-instruct-7b-q4f32 vs rw-stream-13b-8k on partial-output duplication (metric: partial-dup-rate).
- Test B (stop enforcement): inject stop tokens at chunk boundaries and measure time-to-stop (ms) and any trailing garbage tokens.
- Test C (latency): single-user 95th percentile under your network profile (we’ll replay traces).

Deliverables we’ll share:
- Short bench report (CSV attached) with exact token-latency distributions.
- Prioritized anomaly list and recommended configuration: batching window, block dedupe, strict-stop flag recommendation per prompt.
- A small patch to the prompt set with normalized stop variants (attached).

Immediate ask: confirm that your team is OK with Redwood running strict-stop in the POC. It slightly changes the final chunk appearance, but we think it aligns with your requirement to never emit clinician-signature lines.

If OK, I’ll run the tests as soon as the transcripts arrive and send the bench report by EOD Wed (5/26). Would you be available for a 30-minute results call on Thu 5/27 10–11am PT? I’ll send an invite.

Thanks —
Soojin
